{"body":" https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1001 Closes the user report that Codex sessions pile up and have to be cleaned by hand with `entire status` + `entire session stop `. The request was for `entire session stop --older-than=3d`. That treats the symptom — the root cause is fixable at the source, and process death is a better signal than any time threshold. No new flag is included; see "On `--older-than`" below. ## What was wrong **1. Codex never fired a session-end hook.** We registered `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop` and `PostToolUse`. Codex gained a `SessionEnd` hook in 0.146 (openai/codex#33895); we weren't listening, so quitting Codex left the session un-finalized forever. **2. The safety net had an off-by-one-phase bug.** `State.OwnerExited()` gated on `Phase.IsActive()`, which is only `PhaseActive`. An agent that finishes its last turn transitions ACTIVE → IDLE, so a session whose agent then quit was invisible to the dead-owner sweep in `entire status` and `entire doctor`. That is precisely the shape Codex leaves behind — and it can happen to any agent killed before its hook runs. Those sessions lingered as "active" for 7 days until `StaleSessionThreshold` made `StateStore.Load` **delete the state file outright**, discarding pending checkpoint work rather than condensing it. ## Verified against real Codex Same flow run twice, with a binary built at `main` for the baseline: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | session state | `phase: idle`, `ended_at: null` | `phase: ended` | | `entire status` | lists it under **Active Sessions** | nothing lingering | The session-end hook completes in **19ms** against Codex's 3s cap. The safety net was exercised independently by pointing the new binary at the stale pre-fix repo: `Finalized 1 exited session(s) (agent process gone)`, idle → ended. That path covers Codex < 0.146, SIGKILL, and reboot. ## Notable constraint `SessionEnd` runs inside Codex's shutdown, so it is budgeted far more tightly than any other hook: 1s default, **hard 3s cap** (`SESSION_END_MAX_TIMEOUT_SEC`), and on expiry Codex terminates the hook's entire process tree. Asking for more prints a clamping warning at every startup. So hook timeouts became per-event, and the command match now includes the timeout so a hook installed by an older Entire gets rewritten rather than left to nag. Agents in this position declare `agent.SessionEndBudgeter`, which bounds **only** the eager condense — mark-ended is a single atomic rename and always runs to completion, so a session can never be left un-finalized. ## Also fixed here - **A stall this PR would otherwise have introduced.** Widening the sweep to IDLE multiplied its candidate set, and each candidate triggered a deadline-free condense inside `entire status` — ~120ms floor, seconds for a real transcript, serial and uncapped, in a 40ms command. `--json` is what the MCP `entire_status` tool calls, and prints nothing until it returns. `sweepCondenseBudget` now caps condensing across the whole sweep while still marking every candidate ENDED. - **An internal log line leaking into `entire status`.** Neither `status` nor `doctor` initializes logging, so the sweep's `phase transition` line printed raw onto the terminal via `slog.Default()`. Pre-existing, but this PR makes it common. Now routed to `.entire/logs/` — and the level getter is wired, without which the sweep ignored `log_level` in settings. ## On `--older-than` Deliberately not included. Once process death handles this automatically, a time threshold only serves cases where liveness is Unknown: Windows (`proclive` is unsupported there) and cross-host state. Happy to add it if you still want the escape hatch. ## Needs a follow-up decision `codex exec` **now fires hooks** — all five, verified against 0.147.0 — which invalidates a premise `entire review` is built on. All four comments are from the two bots (Cursor Bugbot + Copilot), posted against `4cfc711`. One commit landed after that (`dec49b8c9`), so I checked each against HEAD.

## 1. Cursor — "Codex vanishes after upgrade" (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/hooks.go:237-246`) — still valid

`AreHooksInstalled` still loops over all of `managedHooks` and returns false unless every one is present, and `managedHooks` now includes `SessionEnd`. An existing install with the four older hooks reports not-installed, so Codex drops out of `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` — the `entire status` Agents line (`status.go:194`, and the `agents` JSON field), plus the `entire review` / `entire investigate` agent pickers and the telemetry agent string — until `entire enable` is re-run.

Two things the bot didn't have:
- This is not a semantic change. `main` does the same thing, just spelled as an explicit 4-way AND (`hooks.go:253-256` on main), so the same disappearance happened when `PostToolUse` was added.
- `dec49b8c9` (after the review) added `session_end` to `MissingEntireHooks`, so `entire doctor` now prints "Codex hooks: OUT OF DATE … Run `entire enable`" and names it. Discoverable, but only from `doctor` — `status` still just silently omits Codex.

So: real, unchanged, and a deliberate-looking consequence. The open call is whether to accept it or relax `AreHooksInstalled` to a core subset.

## 2 & 3. Cursor + Copilot — stale logger after the sweep (`logging/logger.go:155-183`, `session_finalize.go:56`) — same bug, both still valid

`Close()` nils `logBufWriter` and `logFile` but leaves `logger` non-nil, and the handler captured the `*bufio.Writer` by value at `createLogger` (`logger.go:204-210`). After `finalizeExitedSessions` returns and its deferred cleanup runs, `log()` still sees `logger != nil`, so it never falls back to `slog.Default` (`logger.go:267-270`) — it writes into an orphaned buffer over a closed file. Lines under 8KB are simply never flushed.

It bites where the command keeps working after the sweep: `entire doctor` then runs `strat.CondenseSessionByID` / `discardSession` per stuck session (`doctor.go:171-213`), and all of that logging is dropped. Note the delta vs `main` is "dropped" rather than "broken" — on main those same lines printed raw onto the terminal via `slog.Default()`, which is the hazard this PR set out to remove.

Careful with the obvious fix: nilling `logger` inside `Close` restores the fallback and puts that terminal noise back for doctor's tail. Hoisting `EnsureInitialized`'s cleanup to command scope in `status.go`/`doctor.go` fixes it without that regression, at the cost of two call sites.

## 4. Copilot — `filterActiveSessions` comment overclaims (`sessions.go:280-283`) — valid, but pre-existing

The comment still asserts parity with `entire status`, and `status.go:438` still filters on `EndedAt == nil` while `filterActiveSessions` uses `!IsEnded()` (`Phase == PhaseEnded || EndedAt != nil`).

The divergence is reachable, not just legacy: `attach.go:694-696` sets `Phase = PhaseEnded` and never stamps `EndedAt`, so a manually attached session shows under status's Active Sessions but is invisible to `session stop`.

What the bot missed is that this PR didn't introduce it — `main`'s predicate is `s.Phase != PhaseEnded && s.EndedAt == nil`, identical to `!IsEnded()`, and main's comment makes the same claim. The PR only reworded it. So it's a pre-existing inconsistency the diff drew attention to; fixing it means switching `status.go:438` to `IsEnded()`, which would also make the comment true.

103	
104		// Codex rollout files are JSONL; the session id lives in the payload of the
105		// first "session_meta" line. Parse line-by-line rather than anchoring a
106		// regex on field order — Codex reorders JSON keys between versions (the old
107		// regex silently stopped matching on Codex 0.142.x). This mirrors the CLI's
108		// own parser in cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/transcript.go.
109		for _, raw := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {

132	// appendCompactedEncryptedHistory appends the two encrypted-payload shapes Entire
133	// has to make replayable, so a resume of the restored transcript exercises both:
134	//
135	//   - a top-level `response_item` whose payload type is `compaction`. Sanitization
136	//     strips its encrypted_content but KEEPS the line, so the stored transcript
137	//     stays line-aligned with the rollout (offsets are counted on the rollout and
138	//     applied to the stored copy). This is the shape that decides whether Codex
139	//     tolerates a compaction item with no payload.
140	//   - a `compacted` line whose replacement_history carries reasoning and compaction
141	//     items. Those nested items are removed outright — they are array elements, so
142	//     removing them cannot shift line numbers.
143	func appendCompactedEncryptedHistory(t *testing.T, rolloutPath string) {
144		t.Helper()
145	
146		lines := []map[string]any{
147			{
148				"timestamp": "2026-04-08T12:00:00.000Z",
149				"type":      "response_item",
150				"payload": map[string]any{

152					"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
153				},

155			{
156				"timestamp": "2026-04-08T12:00:01.000Z",
157				"type":      "compacted",
158				"payload": map[string]any{
159					"message": "",
160					"replacement_history": []map[string]any{
161						{
162							"type": "message",
163							"role": "user",
164							"content": []map[string]any{
165								{"type": "input_text", "text": "hello"},
166							},
167						},
168						{
169							"type":              "reasoning",
170							"summary":           []map[string]any{{"text": "brief"}},
171							"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
172						},
173						{
174							"type":              "compaction",
175							"encrypted_content": "REDACTED",
176						},
177					},
178				},
179			},
180		}

182		f, err := os.OpenFile(rolloutPath, os.O_APPEND|os.O_WRONLY, 0)
183		require.NoError(t, err)
184		defer f.Close()

186		for _, line := range lines {
187			encoded, err := json.Marshal(line)
188			require.NoError(t, err)
189			_, err = f.Write(append(encoded, '\n'))
190			require.NoError(t, err)

194	// findRestoredCodexRollout returns the rollout `entire resume` wrote, which is the one
195	// the subsequent `codex resume` loads.
196	//
197	// Restore may either overwrite the agent's original file or add a second one, and
198	// which happens depends on the machine's timezone: Entire derives the restored path
199	// from the session start time in UTC (codex.restoredRolloutPath), while Codex names
200	// its own rollout in local time. On a UTC host (CI) the two names collide and restore
201	// overwrites in place; anywhere else they differ and both files remain.
202	//
203	// So do not key off "the path that is not the original" — that only holds off-UTC.
204	// Pick the most recently written rollout instead, which is the restored copy in both
205	// layouts.
206	func findRestoredCodexRollout(t *testing.T, codexHome string) string {
207		t.Helper()
208	
209		matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(codexHome, "sessions", "*", "*", "*", "rollout-*.jsonl"))

216		return newest
217	}

219	// newestFile returns the most recently modified of paths. Ties are broken by taking
220	// the later entry, which keeps the choice deterministic when a filesystem reports
221	// coarse timestamps.
222	func newestFile(t *testing.T, paths []string) string {
223		t.Helper()
224		require.NotEmpty(t, paths)

226		newest := paths[0]
227		newestMod := fileModTime(t, newest)

229			if mod := fileModTime(t, p); !mod.Before(newestMod) {
230				newest, newestMod = p, mod
231			}
232		}
233		return newest
234	}

236	func fileModTime(t *testing.T, path string) time.Time {
237		t.Helper()
238		fi, err := os.Stat(path)
239		require.NoError(t, err)
240		return fi.ModTime()
241	}
242	
243	// assertRestoredCompactionStripped verifies the restored rollout carries a
244	// top-level compaction item whose encrypted payload was stripped while its LINE
245	// survived. That is the shape the subsequent `codex resume` has to tolerate, and
246	// asserting it here stops the test from passing vacuously if the fixture, the
247	// sanitizer, or the restore path ever stops producing it.
248	func assertRestoredCompactionStripped(t *testing.T, rolloutPath string) {
249		t.Helper()
250	
251		data, err := os.ReadFile(rolloutPath)
252		require.NoError(t, err)
253		require.NotContains(t, string(data), "encrypted_content",
254			"restored rollout still carries encrypted payloads")
255	
256		var sawStrippedCompaction bool
257		var sawCompactedLine bool
258		for _, raw := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {
259			if len(bytes.TrimSpace(raw)) == 0 {
260				continue
261			}
262			var line struct {
263				Type    string          `json:"type"`
264				Payload json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
265			}
266			if json.Unmarshal(raw, &line) != nil || line.Type != "response_item" {
267				continue
268			}
269			var payload map[string]any
270			if json.Unmarshal(line.Payload, &payload) != nil {
271				continue
272			}
273			if payload["type"] == "compaction" {
274				sawStrippedCompaction = true
275				t.Logf("restored top-level compaction item, payload keys: %v", payloadKeys(payload))
276				require.NotContains(t, payload, "encrypted_content",
277					"compaction item kept its encrypted payload")
278			}
279		}
280	
281		for _, raw := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {
282			if bytes.Contains(raw, []byte(`"type":"compacted"`)) {
283				sawCompactedLine = true
284			}
285		}
286		require.True(t, sawCompactedLine, "restored rollout lost the compacted line")
287	
288		require.True(t, sawStrippedCompaction,
289			"restored rollout has no top-level compaction item — the test did not exercise "+
290				"the payload-less compaction shape, so its result is meaningless")
291	}
292	
293	func payloadKeys(payload map[string]any) []string {
294		keys := make([]string, 0, len(payload))
295		for k := range payload {
296			keys = append(keys, k)
297		}
298		sort.Strings(keys)
299		return keys
300	}
301	
302	// TestFindRestoredCodexRollout_HandlesOverwriteAndSecondFile pins the selection rule
303	// against both layouts `entire resume` can produce, without needing a real agent.
304	//
305	// This exists because the original helper assumed restore always adds a second file
306	// and identified it as "the path that is not the original". That assumption is
307	// timezone-dependent — Entire derives the restored path in UTC while Codex names its
308	// own rollout in local time — so it held on a developer laptop and broke on CI, where
309	// the names collide and restore overwrites in place.
310	func TestFindRestoredCodexRollout_HandlesOverwriteAndSecondFile(t *testing.T) {
311		t.Parallel()
312	
313		write := func(t *testing.T, home, name string, modAt time.Time) string {
314			t.Helper()
315			dir := filepath.Join(home, "sessions", "2026", "08", "06")
316			require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755))
317			p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
318			require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(p, []byte("{}\n"), 0o644))
319			require.NoError(t, os.Chtimes(p, modAt, modAt))
320			return p
321		}
322	
323		base := time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)
324	
325		t.Run("overwritten in place (UTC host)", func(t *testing.T) {
326			t.Parallel()
327			home := t.TempDir()
328			only := write(t, home, "rollout-2026-08-06T10-54-17-sess.jsonl", base)
329	
330			require.Equal(t, only, findRestoredCodexRollout(t, home),
331				"with a single rollout the helper must use it rather than demanding a second file")
332		})
333	
334		t.Run("second file added (non-UTC host)", func(t *testing.T) {
335			t.Parallel()
336			home := t.TempDir()
337			// The agent's own file, named in local time, written first.
338			write(t, home, "rollout-2026-08-06T12-54-17-sess.jsonl", base)
339			// Restore's copy, named in UTC, written afterwards.
340			restored := write(t, home, "rollout-2026-08-06T10-54-17-sess.jsonl", base.Add(time.Minute))
341	
342			require.Equal(t, restored, findRestoredCodexRollout(t, home),
343				"with two rollouts the helper must pick the one restore wrote, not the lexically first")
344		})
345	}

## Gaps & Limitations

- **SessionEnd is tightly budgeted:** 1s default, 3s hard cap, process tree killed on expiry. See "SessionEnd's timeout ceiling" above. This is the only Entire hook that cannot assume it will finish.
- **SessionEnd needs Codex 0.146+:** Added 2026-07-17 (openai/codex#33895), first tagged in `rust-v0.146.0-alpha.3`. On older Codex the hook is simply never called, and such sessions are instead reclaimed by the exited-owner sweep in `entire status` / `entire doctor` (`session.State.OwnerExited`).
- **SessionEnd must be trusted before it fires:** Codex silently skips hooks with no `trusted_hash` entry in the user's `config.toml`. Existing users have trusted the four older events but not `session_end`, so the hook does nothing until they approve it via `/hooks` inside Codex. `HookTrustGaps` and `MissingEntireHooks` both cover `session_end`, so `entire doctor` and the SessionStart banner say so — without that it would fail silently.
- **`reason` carries no information:** always `"other"`, so a session ended by `/clear` is indistinguishable from one ended by quitting.
- **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration handles this gracefully.
- **No hooks fire under `-s read-only`:** verified against 0.147.0 — a `codex exec -s read-only` run produces no hook invocations at all, so no session is tracked. `-s workspace-write` fires the full set.
- **Hook response protocol differs from Claude Code:** Codex uses `systemMessage` (same field name) but also supports `hookSpecificOutput` with `additionalContext` for injecting context into the model. For Entire's purposes, `systemMessage` is sufficient.

All four changes are in and `mise run fmt`/`lint` are green; `test:ci` is still running and I'll report when it lands. The e2e answer turned out to be the interesting part:

## e2e: yes, one change was needed — and it was a silent hole

Nothing in e2e was *skipped* for want of session-end logic — no codex skips, and `WaitForSessionIdle` (the only session-phase helper) waits for "no ACTIVE session", which an ENDED session satisfies. But the new hook would have been **inert for the entire e2e suite**.

`e2e/agents/codex_trust.go` pre-trusts hooks by recomputing Codex's `trusted_hash` values itself, and it enumerates events in three hand-maintained places (`codexHookEvents`, `codexHookEventLabels`, `codexEventGroups`) — none of which knew `SessionEnd`. Since Codex silently skips hooks with no trust entry (the very gate `dec49b8c9` documented), `entire enable` would have written the hook and Codex would never have fired it. No test fails; coverage just quietly isn't there. Fixed all three, plus `TestCodexHookTrustState_CoversEveryInstalledEvent`, which installs hooks for real and requires a trust entry per Entire handler — I verified it fails with the right message when the label is removed.

Two things that make me expect the suite to stay green now that the hook actually fires: `codex exec` ends the session at the end of every `RunPrompt`, and Vogon already fires `session-end` after every run (`e2e/vogon/main.go:87`), so all 60 canary tests already run that shape. The codex-only test that quits the TUI (`codex_resume_test.go`) now hits a real SessionEnd during `Quit` — that's within the 3s cap against its 15s timeout, and resuming an ended session is the normal `entire resume` path.

## The other three

**1. `AreHooksInstalled` loosened** — `managedHook` gained a `core` flag; only the four pre-existing events gate the check, and `SessionEnd`'s absence is drift for `MissingEntireHooks`/`doctor` to report. Worth knowing: this was worse than Bugbot described. Codex's `DetectPresence` delegates to `AreHooksInstalled` (`codex.go:55`), so an upgraded install was neither "installed" nor "detected" — and a non-interactive `entire enable` re-run keeps *currently installed* agents, so it would have dropped Codex instead of repairing it. `entire enable` still repairs the gap because `setupAgentHooks` calls `InstallHooks` unconditionally.

**2/3. Stale logger** — `Close()` now clears `logger`, so a handler can never outlive the buffer it writes into. On its own that would push doctor's post-sweep condense logs back to the terminal, so `finalizeExitedSessions` now returns its cleanup instead of deferring it internally, and `doctor` defers it at command scope. New test asserts a line logged after cleanup reaches `slog.Default()` rather than vanishing.

**4. `IsEnded` parity** — all three `EndedAt` checks in `status.go` now use `IsEnded()`. The divergence was reachable, not just legacy: `attach.go:694` sets `Phase = PhaseEnded` without stamping `EndedAt`, so an attached session showed as active in `status` but `session stop` refused to list it. The `sessions.go` comment Copilot flagged is now true rather than reworded.
